slides.texte_overlay:
7 social hacks that feel
like cheating at work
Starting a new job? Ask "What do you wish someone had told you in your first week?" People love giving advice, you learn the unwritten rules, and you've made an ally before lunch on day one.
Need to push back on your boss? Don't say "That won't work." Say "I can do that. What should I drop to make room?" Same no, but now you sound like the reasonable one in the room.
Someone takes credit for your idea in a meeting? Smile and say "Glad you liked it. When I first pitched it, I was also thinking..." You claim it back calmly, and nobody has to look bad.
Have one interesting thing to say at the coffee machine. Five minutes a day of history, art or science. "Did you know the first webcam was pointed at a coffee pot?" Small talk suddenly gets easy.
slides.texte_sophia: Have one interesting thing to say at the coffee machine. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. Small talk suddenly gets way easier.

slides.texte_overlay: Meeting dragging on forever? Say "So, who's doing what by Friday?" Everyone suddenly gets very clear, the meeting wraps up, and you look like the guy who actually gets things done.
Got a nice compliment from a client? Forward it to your boss with one line. "Thought you'd like to see this." You're not bragging, you're sharing good news, and it's remembered at review time.
Made a mistake? Report it before anyone finds it. "Heads up, I messed up the numbers, here's the fix." Telling people first turns a screw-up into proof that you can be trusted.
